note: Bodies that struck the Earth, drawn by ImpactorLayer on the red layer's distance scale. Each path key point is the body's distance from Earth (log10 metres) at a date (years ago); kind says whether it is measured or schematic. INTERIM values pending the sourced research in Docs/research/impacts.md.

impactors.name: Theia
impactors.blurb: A Mars-sized body that formed in the inner solar system near the young Earth. Its glancing collision made the Moon from the debris.

path.note: a neighbouring orbit, about an AU from Earth

impactors.name: Late Heavy Bombardment
impactors.blurb: A proposed spike of impacts on the inner planets about 4.1 to 3.8 billion years ago, rocks thrown from the asteroid belt as the giant planets moved. Whether it was a spike or a tail is debated.

impactors.name: Chicxulub impactor
impactors.formedLabel: the Chicxulub asteroid forms beyond Jupiter
impactors.lifeLabel: impact winter: about three-quarters of species die, all dinosaurs but birds
impactors.blurb: An asteroid about 10 km wide, of carbonaceous rock that formed beyond Jupiter, waited in the asteroid belt for four and a half billion years, then struck the Yucatan 66 million years ago.

path.note: in the belt until sent toward Earth (when is unknown)
